subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does the documented `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` policy intentionally cover every browser-reachable state-changing Gateway HTTP route, or should authenticated loopback HTTP routes also require a separate anti-CSRF token?
rationale: Source and docs establish existing origin and authentication defenses, but choosing whether origin validation alone is the product security boundary—or whether a second token is mandatory—requires maintainers to define the supported browser, proxy, CLI, and local-client contract.

options.title: Audit and centralize origin enforcement
options.body: Inventory all state-changing HTTP routes and enforce the existing browser-origin policy through one shared pre-dispatch guard, adding route-level tests for any uncovered path.

options.title: Require a separate CSRF token
options.body: Add a browser-session anti-CSRF token on top of Gateway authentication and origin checks, accepting the client and compatibility work this creates.

options.title: Close after negative verification
options.body: Close only if a current-main route audit and concrete cross-origin requests show that every relevant route already rejects the alleged attack.

recommendation.title: Audit and centralize origin enforcement
recommendation.body: Inventory all state-changing HTTP routes and enforce the existing browser-origin policy through one shared pre-dispatch guard, adding route-level tests for any uncovered path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from recent Gateway security-boundary work and were explicitly mentioned in the issue timeline.
